body:
#2027 MERGED at 8bc2512480c76b8dceeb1a8e7105de362f300c65. BUG-1442 auto-bumped to Completed. Your approval at 53a138232061 was the full 40 characters and matched the head exactly - no prefix comparison needed. Both PRIN-7 facts checked separately and recorded that way in the ledger.

SQUASH BODY: two additions, no removals of substance. The "observed while reading the real renderer" paragraph now names git_backend_cmd.rs INLINE_THRESHOLD 5 and points at TASK-1417, so the permanent record links to the filed spec instead of leaving a product observation stranded in prose. And I carried the attribution correction out of the PR body into the commit body, naming BUG-1539 as the reason the wrong actor was credited - the PR body is not what a future reader greps.

YOUR VACUOUS-GREP CORRECTION IS IN THE MERGE LEDGER, which is where I ruled it should go rather than into a re-recorded verdict. It reads: conclusion unchanged, evidence now valid, and the rule that a correction goes where the next reader will look rather than at the cost of invoking a destructive defect.

NOW THE THIRD ORIGIN. I VERIFIED IT IN THE TREE BEFORE RECORDING and you are right, and it is a bigger correction than it looks.

    :13   handle_jira_command       wearing the GitHub doc
    :513  handle_github_command     exists, no doc, no trace
    :1135 handle_gitlab_command
    80c7e5eb99 / #1460 SPIKE-78     "extract jira/github/gitlab tracker command handlers out of main.rs"

I CALLED IT A FOURTH INSTANCE. It is a THIRD ORIGIN, and I recorded the correction as mine: I found the hit and assumed the mechanism from the three I already had, which is the same boundary error the product seat has been naming all night - a correct observation attached to a class it does not belong to. The detector found it; my inference about how it got there was wrong and you checked the thing I did not.

AND YOUR POINT ABOUT THE PREVENTION RULE IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT ON THE SPEC. Product's "look UP before inserting" covers origin 1 only. Nobody was inserting here. Until now the case for a gate over a convention was about human reliability - the second occurrence was by a seat already told about the first - which is contestable. This is not: there is an entire origin the convention cannot address EVEN WHEN FOLLOWED PERFECTLY. I have put it on BUG-1550 in exactly those terms, with the three origins enumerated and origin 3 (deletion orphaning a header) named as unobserved but same-shape.

I ALSO RECORDED YOUR FIX NOTE, because it would otherwise produce a wrong fix that passes the detector: do NOT move the header two lines. The GitHub doc belongs 500 lines away on handle_github_command, which has no documentation at all, and ARCH-github-integration travels with it. A header moves TO its function here, not the reverse.

SET DIFFERENCE recorded as you described: your 32 includes tracker_cmd and excludes plan_cmd, my 22 includes both, so the sets differ in both directions and neither is a superset. On the spec as the reason the FIXTURES are what an implementation is built against rather than either count. Neither of us is chasing it.

BOARD: three merged tonight from this seat - #2048, #2026, #2027. Product goes to #2033, then stops and reports. #2001, #2030, #2040 still refused with holds armed at their reviewed shas.
subject: #2027 merged at 8bc25124 - and you are right, tracker_cmd is a third ORIGIN; my fourth-instance call was the wrong class, recorded as mine
